  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Decision Analysis with Uncertain Outcomes}

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(risk.decision)
```

This one-stage decision model compares project alternatives under uncertain
demand. Its invented data illustrate decision-tree reasoning in the style of
Howard and Abbas, rather than reproducing a specific published example.

```{r}
path <- system.file("extdata", "project_selection.csv", package = "risk.decision")
projects <- import_risk_data(path)
decision_tree_summary(projects, threshold = 0)
sensitivity_analysis(projects, alternative = "Innovative", branch = 3,
                     probabilities = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7))
generate_risk_matrix(projects, ylab = "Net benefit (arbitrary units)")
```

The sensitivity calculation changes the probability of low demand for the
innovative project and redistributes the remainder proportionally across its
other branches. It does not simultaneously change the conservative project,
even if the underlying demand uncertainty is shared.

For a separate, deterministic multi-attribute illustration, suppose stakeholders
have already scored financial and strategic performance from 0 to 1 and
elicited weights that describe trade-offs over those full scales:

```{r}
attribute_path <- system.file("extdata", "attribute_values.csv", package = "risk.decision")
attributes <- read.csv(attribute_path)
value_function(attributes, c(financial_value = 0.6, strategic_value = 0.4))
```

The additive model follows the multi-attribute value-modeling approach
associated with Keeney and Raiffa. Additivity requires suitable preferential
independence and properly elicited scale weights. These illustrative scores
are not utilities under uncertainty and are not combined with the monetary
outcome model above.
